title: A finite algebra over a Nagata ring is Nagata
statement: Let $R$ be a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings making $S$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $S$ is a Nagata ring: $S$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ the domain $S/\mathfrak q$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. In particular, for every ideal $I\subseteq R$ the quotient ring $R/I$ is a Nagata ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032T (lemma-quasi-finite-over-nagata, line 45703), in the case of a finite ring map named there ('quasi-finite ring map (for example finite)'); the quotient R -> R/I is finite, generated by 1

proof.text: Since R is Nagata [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], it is Noetherian. A finite R-algebra T is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. For each prime q of T, put p = q.comap(algebraMap R T); p is prime. The canonical map R/p -> T/q is injective (Ideal.algebraMap_quotient_injective). Quotienting finite module generators makes T/q finite over R; the compatible scalar tower R -> R/p -> T/q and Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite make it finite over R/p [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The quotient R/p is Noetherian by the same finite-algebra lemma and N-2 by the Nagata hypothesis.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032T (lemma-quasi-finite-over-nagata), proof, lines 45708-45717; finite case

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-n2-ascends-finite-domain-extension] to the injective finite extension of domains R/p -> T/q, with their canonical fraction fields. It gives IsN2 (T/q) (FractionRing (T/q)) for each prime q. Together with Noetherianity from step 1 this proves IsNagataRing T [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. This reuses exactly the fraction-field and integral-closure argument of the former steps 2 and 3 through the existing N-2 ascent theorem.

proof.text: Specialize the finite-algebra assertion to T = S. For each ideal I of R, the quotient R/I is a finite R-module generated by 1 [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (Mathlib Module.Finite quotient instance); specialize the same assertion to T = R/I. Pair the two conclusions to obtain the unchanged theorem.

split_report.summary: Split the finite case of Stacks 032T by writing out the finite-domain proof of 032I. For every prime quotient S/q, the contracted quotient A=R/p is an N-2 Noetherian domain and B=S/q is finite over A. Its fraction field L is finite over Frac(A); for each finite M/L the integral closures of A and B in M agree because B/A is integral. N-2 makes this common closure finite over A, hence over B. The quotient R/I is generated by 1 and follows as a special case. Reused only existing Mathlib leaves and definitions; no new node was needed.
